skill.name: nature-paper-card
skill.description: Build a source-grounded deep-reading Paper Card for one scientific paper, preprint, PDF, DOI, arXiv page, publisher article, or pasted paper text. Use when the user asks for a Paper Card, deep-reading literature card, single-paper deep analysis, module-by-module analysis, experiment-to-claim evidence chain, conclusion-boundary audit, critical analysis, knowledge connections, or candidate research ideas. Produce the fixed Sections 01-16 covering bibliographic position, research question, background route, pain point, core insight, method and module logic, essential formulas, experiment-to-claim evidence, conclusion boundaries, author-stated limitations, critical analysis, learned knowledge, knowledge connections, and testable research ideas. Do not use for full-paper bilingual translation, formal peer-review reports, batch literature monitoring, academic-English collection, comprehension quizzes, or public-article writing.
skill.summary: Create a 16-section, source-grounded analysis card for one scientific paper.
skill.author: yuan1z0825

content.user_title: Analyze One Scientific Paper as an Evidence Card
content.value_statement: Scientific papers are difficult to evaluate when claims, methods, and evidence are scattered across sections. This skill creates a structured, traceable Paper Card with explicit limits.
actual_capabilities: Produces a fixed 16-section Markdown card for one scientific paper.
Classifies methods, discovery, resource, clinical, materials, and review papers.
Links central claims to figures, tables, equations, experiments, and source locations.
Separates paper statements, external facts, analysis, hypotheses, and user judgments.
Audits card structure, locator use, evidence coverage, and research idea fields.
Marks unsupported content as not applicable or not assessable.
limitations: It analyzes one paper at a time and does not monitor literature in batches.
Scientific correctness still requires human review because automated checks focus on structure and traceability.
Abstract-only or partial input produces a limited card without unseen methods or results.
External field history and novelty claims remain unverified unless targeted research is performed.

use_cases.title: Deep Reading for Study
use_cases.description: Turn one assigned paper into structured notes with methods, evidence, limitations, and reusable concepts.

use_cases.title: Evidence Review for Research
use_cases.description: Trace each major claim to experiments, figures, tables, formulas, and bounded conclusions.

use_cases.title: Paper Screening for Teams
use_cases.description: Create a consistent card that helps a research team compare a paper with current project needs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Paper Card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Paper Card for this attached PDF. Use only the supplied paper, cite evidence locations, and mark unsupported sections as not assessable.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a complete paper PDF.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Paper by Identifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this DOI or arXiv paper as a Paper Card. Verify bibliographic details, explain the method, and connect each central claim to evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate analysis from a public paper identifier.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Claims and Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Paper Card focused on the experiment-to-claim chain. Separate author claims from supported conclusions, alternative explanations, limitations, and missing controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced critical analysis for research planning.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Hybrid Contribution
prompt_templates.prompt: Treat this paper as methods-primary and resource-secondary. Audit both contribution types, preserve the fixed sections, and propose testable ideas with failure conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis of a paper with two contribution types.

output_examples.input: A complete PDF describing a new machine learning method with ablation studies.
output_examples.output: A 16-section Markdown card traces the method, formulas, baselines, ablations, and reported gains to specific paper locations.

output_examples.input: An abstract and bibliographic metadata for a clinical study.
output_examples.output: A source-limited card summarizes the stated question and result while marking unseen methods, tables, limitations, and causal claims as not assessable.

output_examples.input: A source map for a paper with missing page locators and several figures.
output_examples.output: A structure-grounded card cites stable sections and figure identifiers without inventing page numbers, then records locator limitations in the evidence status.

best_practices: Provide the full paper, figures, tables, and supplements when available.
State whether external verification is allowed for history, bibliography, or novelty checks.
Review numerical results and scientific interpretations against the original source before reuse.
anti_patterns: Do not request unsupported conclusions from an abstract-only source.
Do not treat author novelty claims as independent prior-art verification.
Do not use this skill for batch monitoring, full translation, or formal peer review.

faq.question: What inputs can this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It accepts one paper as a PDF, DOI, arXiv page, publisher article, source map, or pasted text.

faq.question: Does it summarize several papers together?
faq.answer: No. It creates one deep-reading card for one paper and does not perform batch synthesis.

faq.question: Can it work from an abstract only?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates a source-limited card and marks unseen methods, evidence, and limitations as not assessable.

faq.question: Does it verify novelty claims?
faq.answer: Only when targeted external research is performed. Otherwise, novelty and field-history claims are clearly marked as unverified.

faq.question: What files does it produce?
faq.answer: The main output is a Markdown Paper Card. PDF workflows also produce a source bundle and an audit report.

faq.question: Does the automated audit prove scientific correctness?
faq.answer: No. It checks structure, source locators, and evidence coverage, while scientific interpretation still requires expert review.
